findings.evidence: Both fetch functions followed a 302 from an approved loopback fixture to a denied hostname. Each target received one request and its response was accepted. This proves a policy bypass in the reusable fetch API; external deployment exposure was not tested.
findings.acceptance: Producer repair refuses redirects; preserve direct-fetch success, then publish, upgrade consumers and verify their network policy.

findings.evidence: Main resource extraction calls NIP-98; production Bearer is refused and DPoP has no dispatch. Its challenge nevertheless advertises both. The valid Nostr control reads private bytes; the ES256 OIDC/DPoP pair passes library checks but receives 401.
findings.acceptance: Compose the selected OIDC profile into real resource admission, including proof, issuer authority, audience, replay and WAC, and pass an external-client journey.

findings.evidence: `normalise_htu` lower-cases the path and trims trailing slashes. A valid proof for `/Foo` verifies against `/foo` and `/Foo/`, while adding a query causes refusal.
findings.acceptance: Compare parsed URI components according to the selected DPoP contract, with case-distinct resources and query-bearing requests tested. No resource-route bypass is claimed.

findings.evidence: With capacity one, a valid second proof evicts the first unexpired `jti`; the unchanged first proof then verifies again. The IdP supplies this cache during token exchange, before code consumption.
findings.acceptance: Retain admission records for the remaining acceptance window and define saturation behaviour. Single-use authorisation codes are a separate defence; this probe does not prove duplicate token issuance. Default-TTL timing remains unexecuted.

findings.evidence: The profile helper accepts a literal compact issuer property despite an unrelated subject and a context assigning that prefix elsewhere. Equivalent Turtle is refused. The cached token verifier does not call this helper, and no external-resource consumer was found in the reviewed crate family.
findings.acceptance: Bind the exact WebID subject and expanded issuer predicate through the estate's RDF tooling, support the chosen profile representations, and verify the actual consumer composition.

findings.evidence: Real ES256 tokens with `exp == now` or future `nbf` pass. A `https://`-only WebID passes the prefix test; a non-URL WebID silently falls back to `sub`. Wrong audience and expired-by-one-second controls fail.
findings.acceptance: Correct time and identity-shape policy with deterministic fixtures and explicit compatibility decisions. These are verifier observations, not a demonstrated route takeover.

findings.evidence: Alpha.8 prose claimed arbitrary audiences while current code and test C1 enforce `solid` or an explicit policy. A passing matrix suite had not prevented prose drift.
findings.acceptance: Corrected in the baseline, matrix, ADR extension and test commentary. Preserve source-version and evidence boundaries on future updates.

review_findings.evidence_limit: Inherited proxy and direct pin mechanism confirmed in pinned reqwest source; no proxy rebinding runtime experiment.
Uncapped json body buffering confirmed in source; no memory exhaustion experiment.
HashMaps retain expired entries and have no size bound; no load experiment.
Detailed library errors confirmed; client-visible disclosure is inconclusive and main resource OIDC route is unwired.
JWKS miss calls uncached discovery; confirmed by call path, no latency benchmark.
